title: Judgment and the Two Presences of Christ
english: He is compared to irrational cattle, like a female horse having become so and having imitated the impulses of all other irrational animals. He was not made like irrational cattle, having hope if he wishes to be made like God. For there shall be five above the cities and ten the upright in the time to come (Ps 48:15b). And Solomon in the Proverbs says the same thing: A wealthy man hastens to be rich, and he does not know that mercy will hold him.

If even the aforementioned things have happened to the majority of men, nevertheless God will take my soul from the hand of the slave holding it and desiring to swallow it (Ps 48:16). And since the sinner is in slavery according to his condition, the one forgiving those holding him in sins thanks God having received his soul from the hand of the slave.

The one lying before us rich, not knowing another life in his life, thinks by this to bless his soul; and only then does he confess that it is good to him through the giving of material desires (Ps 48:19). A father having begotten him through evil works and a clumsy intellect (Ps 48:20). Likewise, acting toward them, he imitated the parents, and as being similar to the generation of the fathers, he will enter into the same deep abyss of ignorance as they. For having accepted only the present life, he did not hasten to see the light; therefore it has been said regarding the age not to approach it; for perhaps, having been condemned in outer darkness, he will not be permitted to behold the eternal light.

He says [the gods are] not the idols and the demons, but the men partaking of the words of God; for those are gods to whom the word of God came. God the Lord is of these gods, just as he is king of kings. And again, from the rising of the sun even unto the settings, he says, to know what... From Zion the splendor of his beauty has come. For the one according to the flesh was shown from the seed of David. The God of the gods himself, having called all the earth to partake of him, will not hide nor be forgotten, but will manifest clearly according to the second presence in glory with his angels; and he will not be silent.

Thus, each one is judged according to his works and his practice. It should be noted that in this present word, both presences of Christ are shown: the first through the 'Out of Zion' glory, and the second through 'God has appeared manifestly' (Ps 49:4).

Since the giving of the law is given upon witnesses, heaven and earth, as it is written in Deuteronomy, it is necessary that the people, being distinguished upon the witnesses through whom they received the law, be examined having stood upon the divine laws. He calls not the heaven above, that is, the divine powers, and the earth, I say, the inhabitants upon it, so that those made his children upon it might be exposed: 'Hear, O heaven, and pay attention, O earth, for the children of God are being proclaimed; for they, having received the law upon you, did not keep it' (Ps 49:4).

Perhaps he commands angels to holy men, so that he might gather his pious ones to prepare and establish his covenant of God upon spiritual sacrifices: namely, the sacrifice of praise and if anyone else similar. He commands the pious ones to be gathered to him, receiving the spiritual covenant upon which they are to offer the sacrifices, so that they might fulfill the things foretold.
'The heavens announce so-called righteousness' (Ps 49:6a), [being] men who are holy, bearing the image of the heavenly.

'God examines not the things themselves offered to those approaching, but the disposition according to which they approach' (Ps 49:8); and indeed, he exposes Cain for not having divided the offering rightly. If someone offers a spiritual sacrifice as whole burnt offerings through his whole body, let him do this with right intention; for one is not praised for the things being done, but one is examined for the intention not being rightly fulfilled.

'Since those in your land, figuratively called bulls, have become hostile to the Savior, concerning whom it is said, "Many bulls have surrounded me, wild oxen have enclosed me"' (Ps 49:9-11a); for this reason, I will not receive them, nor the rams associated with them. For they, offering themselves on behalf of sin, are no better than those who sin. Know then what those who were once beasts of the forest, men awakened from the Gentiles, are to me, being made subject to the divine teaching.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Integrity of the Heart and Speech
english: They have become previously unfruitful, for the grove is a symbol of this. But also the cattle, being like the sheep of Christ, and the oxen who have gone up over your fence—that is, trampling the shadow of the law in the dogmas of the gospel (because of the height they do not reach)—are our own possession. Does Paul say that the care of the oxen matters to God, he who sets forth the law concerning the ox in the books? Or is he speaking certainly about us? But also the souls that have become lofty, being winged by right thoughts and activities, are being called things of the heaven; for I know them, for I know those who belong to me.

The good land that has received the seed, that is, a right heart, having cast the seed thrown by Jesus and having borne fruit, a hundred and sixty, thirty, possessing a full and ripe fruit, is the beauty of the field, not far from the sower; for he says, 'The beauty of the field is with me' (Ps 49:11b). The Savior hungers for the salvation of some; as for the lack of concern for the salvation of the Samaritan woman, he says to the disciples, 'I have food to eat which you do not know' (John 6:32), and 'My food is to do the will of him who sent me' (John 4:34). Since those coming from circumcision approach him with the sensible worship of the shadow as one starving, he says, 'If I hunger, it is not for you'; for the glorious church, which has become mine, is inhabiting the world and its fullness. And the fullness of it is the gospel, not the type, the shadow. Being nourished by the fullness of the Gentiles, I will not demand from you food according to the shadow; but if you wish to have me as your God who heals with the Spirit, sacrifice to me a sacrifice of praise, of thanksgivings and theologizing; for these I receive as offerings; for I desire mercy, not sacrifice, and the knowledge of God more than burnt offerings (Ps 49:14).

He is the same God who is both Most High and a deliverer from distress (Ps 49:14). Regarding praise, he says to offer a sacrifice of thanksgiving   that befit you, and regarding prayers, the promises; for he says both in the first and twentieth [Psalm], 'I will render my thanksgivings in the presence of those who fear him' (Ps 49:12). Since praise is not beautiful in the mouth of a sinner (Ps 49:16), God strikes the one sinning, saying, 'Why do you not recount my righteous decrees, so that you may fulfill them, and why do you take up the...'

Did you receive my covenant in your mouth? For it is necessary that, having received it in your heart and having imprinted the thoughts according to it upon yourself, you would not utter the words of my covenant in this way. To this, the one proclaiming 'do you steal?' agrees, and the following (Ps 49:18–21).

And regarding the mind, 'you will think and not thus'; if ever you were observing someone stealing the will of the truth with heterodox opinion, you were agreeing and running together with him; but also those attempting to commit adultery with the bride of Christ, to draw the ecclesiastical souls toward them, by being of like mind with them or not turning away from those committing adultery, you are placing your part with them. You say this word is fitting for those who are indeed ecclesiastical, but for those coming into fellowship who are not ecclesiastical men.

'Your mouth has increased wickedness.' He who is ignorant of the good but does the evil, he sins; but he who, after knowing the good, sins, is rebuked for wickedness; therefore also the servant who knew the will of his master and does not do it will be beaten much. And it can be 'not thus'; because having taken up the covenant of God through the mouth, if the heart is full of sin, from the abundance of a wicked heart, being in the mouth, it increases in wickedness, just as through his tongue he is wise to entangle with deceits the heretical words that are sophisms.

'Sitting against your brother you have spoken, and against the son of your mother you have set a stumbling block.' Regarding the word 'brother', one can be of like mind and of the same fatherland; but regarding 'son of a mother', one is of the same womb and not from the father. He who is not thus toward brothers, what other can he be able to love?

And regarding the mind: since the word is toward a Jew, perceptibly offering burnt offerings and sacrifices to God, regarding this it must be said to be spoken in the presence of God, 'Sitting'. O you, regarding the letter of the law, you speak against your brother who is according to the spirit of the law and living by it; and you are also against the one who is the son of your mother; for from the same intention the spirit and the letter of the law were issued. And you scandalize the son of the mother, having set a stumbling block and a scandal, the circumcision which is a way of shadow and flesh. Having done these things, and
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: David's Repentance and the Pattern of the Saints
english: I was silent. The silence of God is called the longsuffering toward sinners; for if He were to punish them immediately by those things, He would not be silent, deciding against them, whereas they ought to suffer. This is the mindset held by the 'I have been silent from eternity, and I will not always be silent and endure,' says the Lord (Ps 102:2). He does not say this to the one being reproved: 'These sins have been foretold to you, and I was silent, giving a space from afar through silence and longsuffering for repentance.' It is necessary to be benefited by such silence; from the opposite, you received lawlessness toward the wicked, by which you imagine me to be like you; for you, having glorified me, rejoice that I do not come forth against you.

Those who, having taken up the forgetfulness of God through sluggishness, take hold of understanding, stand upon the spoken words: 'What I longsuffer toward sins, I do not rejoice in, nor do I do this as an evil man, but as an occasion for repentance through goodness and innate kindness, by setting aside punishment' (Ps 50:1). For if you will not choose to understand, the law or the lawlessness seizes, and there is no one rescuing; for God will rescue those who understand and have repented from evil. Let those who confess not care about those who have ceased and are no longer acting, confessing, saying: 'We have sinned, we have done wrong, we have been ungodly' (Ps 50:2). For it is not the one currently doing these things who confesses.

That is, the one praising and theologizing the beauty of God glorifies Him; for the sensory [worship] rather dishonors, bringing God in by making Him manifest and in need of movement. The way is not there in sensory worship, but there in the truth which encounters beauty, which God shows by illuminating His own salvation, the only-begotten Son the Savior, who is the salvation itself; for the salvation of God at times signifies the salvation, and at times the Savior Christ. But let this not become an occasion to rise up against David; for when God has justified, there is no one condemning. But he will be pious toward the man, having understood that the man is long-lived and has spent most of his years in powers and in kingship, introducing only this one sin, having done it, and in addition to this, having counted the people contrary to the will of God, but not even persistently...

For such a great and far-reaching king was rebuked in sin, that when he was rebuked by a private man, he not only did not feel indignation, but even made himself worse, as the rebuking prophet says: 'And the Lord showed your sin' (Ps 51:5). For to say that the Lord showed it is to say that David himself, having led himself to most intense repentance, was led to his sin. We say that what other men fall into when sinning, the saints, running the race of salvation, if ever they should stumble as men inattentive, do not fall but persist in the race, as if the instability of the race had not seemed to them likely to trip them up. And for many other ineffective things the sins of the saints were written down in this regard; for since they are called to imitate an exceeding virtue, being hesitant, they made a pretext for having a divine portion and for the saints being unendurable in sin, but not being such, they were unable to imitate the far-reaching saints. Thus Providence granted a pretext for sin to have occurred concerning them, so that just as they are teachers of virtue, so also they are teachers of repentance for those being instructed then, having done such things. Perhaps also those far-reaching saints, having reached the height of virtue, did not arrive at this by their own power but by the cooperation of God. If they were not to fall, the divine grace would have been little, so that, having slipped, they might seek the helper of their own weakness, having come to be through consciousness (Ps 50:1,2).

And this psalm was not written in vain for Pentecost. For the number has a harmony toward mercy and forgiveness, since, if the writing spirit maintained the sequence of history, it arranged the first Pentecost and the hundredth and those following. For the first Pentecost has an inscription containing the slander of Doeg the Edomite; but that history is before the kingship of David. And the third Pentecost, the slander of the Ziphites against Saul concerning David as being hidden among them, contains this; and this narrative happened before the kingship of David, but the encounter with Bathsheba happened while David was reigning. If not the sequence...
